Using semantic technologies we integrate multiple autonomous systems (e.g. production system, supply chain management and open data). The outcome of real-time data analytics is used in combination with machine learning models trained over historical data in order to precisely forecast production in a manufacturing unit in real time. We also present our key findings and challenges faced while deploying our solution in real industrial settings for a large manufacturing unit. © 2019 IEEE.
Guo X.; Yang Z.; Sun J.	2022	The COVID-19 pandemic and trade frictions impact the continuity of supply chain (SC) operations. Lu Z.X.; Chen J.C.; Ma S.M.	2021	Hydropower is a kind of clean energy with sustainable development. Hydropower generation has strong periodic regularity, so the prediction and control of power generation are particularly important. Real-time and accurate hydroelectric power generation forecasting is a key issue in the energy industry. In this paper, the time series analysis method of ARIMA (p, d, 0) model structure is used for data preprocessing, and the ARIMA (2, 1, 2) model was finally constructed by identification, model comparison, and testing. After comparison, it can be seen that compared with linear regression and exponential prediction models, the ARIMA model has good data fit and adequate extraction. The prediction method is simple and concise, and the short-term prediction is accurate, which can better adapt to the cyclicality of hydropower generation in all seasons. The model predicts the hydroelectric power generation of Guangxi in 2020 to be 5.3 billion kWh in May, 5.5 billion kWh in June, 41 kWh in July, 40 kWh in August, and 36 kWh in September. Based on this forecast, it can be seen that Guangxi's hydroelectric power generation will continue to develop in a sustainable trend, and its quantitative forecast results will provide Guangxi with the energy industry and provide useful references for production planning and industrial layout. © 2021, The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd.
Stekelorum R.; Laguir I.; Lai K.-H.; Gupta S.; Kumar A.	2021	Recent years have seen a growing interest in the separate areas of responsible governance mechanisms and circular economy practices. However, the literature lacks evidence on supplier capabilities as a responsible governance mechanism pathway for buyer firms to improve their circular economy practices. Drawing on the natural resource-based view, and the dynamic capabilities perspective, this study examines suppliers’ supply chain ambidexterity and big data predictive analytics capabilities as enabling factors in support of buyer firms’ responsible governance mechanism for circular economy practices improvements. Using data from surveys conducted among 404 firms (202 focal firm-supplier dyads), the results suggest that the focal firm's supplier-selection mechanism significantly and positively influences its circular economy practices while the supplier-development mechanism has no such effect. We find further that the governance mechanisms vary in their effects on suppliers’ supply chain ambidexterity and subsequent big data analytics capabilities and circular economy practices improvements outcomes. In sum, our findings provide unique insights into the role of suppliers’ capabilities for responsible governance mechanisms to circular economy practices improvements from the perspective of the dyad. © 2021 Elsevier Ltd

Over the last ten years, advances in technology and data collection systems have resulted in the generation of huge volumes of data on a wide variety of topics and at great speed. This paper reviews the impact that this explosion of data is having on product forecasting and how it is improving it. While much of this review will focus on time series data, we will also explore how such data can be used to obtain insights into consumer behavior, and the impact of such data on organizational forecasting. © 2018 International Institute of Forecasters
Tan N.D.; Yu H.C.; Long L.N.B.; You S.-S.	2022	Coffee has long become a familiar and famous drink all over the world. Due to supply chain disruptions, the coffee market is vibrant and changing rapidly. In this article, the time series data on world coffee price will be analysed by using data analytics such as Lyapunov exponent (LE), entropy, and Hurst exponent (HE). By denoising time series data using wavelet decomposition, the echo state network (ESN) model is presented for forecasting time series data. When the coffee commodity price is fluctuating and affecting to production planning and scheduling of supply chain management under market uncertainty, it is necessary to improve the accuracy and efficiency of the prediction method by employing the grey wolf optimisation (GWO) algorithm. By employing the hybrid technique, the predictive analytics models could efficiently estimate the actual prices. The GWO algorithm enhances a machining learning model’s performance for ensuring optimal forecasting with increased accuracy. Copyright © 2022 Inderscience Enterprises Ltd.

Data-driven methods, with predictive model to analyze various industrial data, have been received considerable attention in recent years. However, to get an accurate prediction, it is an essential issue to extract quality features from industrial data, including several variables generated from supply chain and time-variant machining process. In this article, a data-driven method based on wide-deep-sequence (WDS) model is proposed to provide a reliable quality prediction for industrial process with different types of industrial data. To process industrial data of high redundancy, in this article, data reduction is first conducted on different variables by different techniques. Also, an improved wide-deep (WD) model is proposed to extract quality features from key time-invariant variables. Meanwhile, an long short-term memory (LSTM)-based sequence model is presented for exploring quality information from time-domain features. Under the joint training strategy, these models will be combined and optimized by a designed penalty mechanism for unreliable predictions, especially on reduction of defective products. Finally, experiments on a real-world manufacturing process data set are carried out to present the effectiveness of the proposed method in product quality prediction.  © 2012 IEEE.

It's normal to feel overwhelmed when starting a new major, especially in a challenging field like psychology. Here are some tips on managing your time, workload, and adapting to your new environment:

1. Prioritize and set goals: Make a list of the tasks you need to complete and determine their importance. Set goals for what you want to achieve weekly, and break them down into daily objectives.

2. Create a schedule: Make a weekly timetable that includes your classes, study time, breaks, and social activities. Stick to this schedule as closely as possible.

5. Seek help when needed: If you're struggling with the material or workload, don't hesitate to ask your professors, teaching assistants, or classmates for help. Many universities also offer tutoring or academic support centers.

6. Manage your stress: Practice relaxation techniques, such as deep breathing, meditation, or yoga, to help manage stress. Ensure you get enough sleep, eat healthily, and exercise regularly to maintain your well-being.

7. Participate in social and extracurricular activities: Join clubs, attend events, or participate in group study sessions to meet new people and forge connections. This will help you build a support network and make your experience at university more enjoyable.

8. Be patient with yourself: Adapting to a new environment and workload takes time. Be kind to yourself and understand that it's normal to feel overwhelmed. Focus on making progress rather than striving for perfection.

```python
from tkinter import *
from tkinter.filedialog import askopenfilename
from pdf2image import convert_from_path
import tempfile

class PDFViewer:
    def __init__(self, parent):
        self.parent = parent
        self.canvas = None
        self.scrollbar = None
        self.img_list = []
        self.current_img = None
        self.load_button = Button(self.parent, text="Load PDF", command=self.load_pdf)
        self.load_button.pack()
    
    def load_pdf(self):
        pdf_file = askopenfilename(filetypes=[("PDF Files", "*pdf")])
        if pdf_file:
            with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as path:
                images = convert_from_path(pdf_file, output_folder=path, fmt="jpeg")
                self.img_list = images
                self.current_img = images[0]
                self.create_canvas()
                
    def create_canvas(self):
        # create canvas and scrollbar
        self.canvas = Canvas(self.parent, width=self.current_img.size[0], height=self.current_img.size[1])
        self.scrollbar = Scrollbar(self.parent, orient=VERTICAL, command=self.canvas.yview)
        self.canvas.configure(yscrollcommand=self.scrollbar.set)
        self.scrollbar.pack(side=RIGHT, fill=Y)
        self.canvas.pack(side=LEFT, fill=BOTH, expand=1)
        
        # create image on canvas
        self.canvas_img = self.canvas.create_image(0, 0, anchor=NW, image=self.current_img)
        
        # bind canvas to mousewheel scroll

cost but finds the flexibility of the onshore supplier very attractive. The challenge is to value the

To better compare the two suppliers, management identifies demand and exchange rates as the two

توکن بومی آن، SOL، در سال 2021 رشد قابل توجهی را در ارزش شاهد شد و به بیش از 250 دلار رسید، قبل از اینکه در دسامبر 2021 پس از سقوط FTX به 8 دلار برسد. این ارزش سپس به بیش از 20 دلار افزایش یافت اما نتوانست در برابر بروزرسانی‌های امیدبخش مانند توانایی درخشان کردن چندین NFT با هزینه‌های بسیار پایین بطور قابل توجهی افزایش یابد... پس چرا رشد شاهد نیست؟

بزرگترین مشکل سولانا

مشکل اصلی سولانا، فراتر از خروجی‌های بسیاری از شبکه که سرمایه‌گذاران را ترغیب به استفاده از زنجیره‌های دیگر می‌کند، این است که سولانا تنها پلتفرم بلاکچین نیست که معاملات سریع و ارزان ارائه می‌کند. رقبایی نظیر زنجیره هوشمند بایننس (BNB) و پلیگون (MATIC) نیز ویژگی‌های مشابهی ارائه داده و از خروجی‌های متعدد مانند سولانا رنج نبرده است. زنجیره‌های لایه‌دو مبتنی بر اتریوم (ETH) مانند آربیتروم نیز معاملات نسبتاً ارزان و سریع را بدون قطع شبکه ارائه می‌دهند.

به طور خلاصه، اینکه سولانا یک پروژه اغراق آمیز است یا نه به دیدگاه‌های شخصی و ترجیحات بستگی دارد. این پروژه قطعاً توجه زیادی را به خود جلب کرده و ویژگی‌های قابل تحسینی دارد، اما تنها پلتفرم بلاکچین نیست که معاملات سریع و ارزان را ارائه می‌دهد.

assistant_message:
Title: The Great Messy

Setting: 1990s, a suburban family home kitchen, during a fun neighborhood potluck party

INT. SIMMONS FAMILY KITCHEN - DAY

We enter a busy, well-lit, and colorful family kitchen. Friends and neighbors are gathered, and laughter fills the air. The main characters are LUCINDA SIMMONS, the eccentric, stylish, and wise matriarch of the family and her best friend, CHARLENE JONES, a curvy, sassy, larger-than-life woman who's sarcasm and wit are unmatched in the entire neighborhood.

Lucinda stands in the center of the kitchen, dressed tastefully in a vibrant high-waist floral maxi skirt, a pastel-colored blouse, pearls, large golden hoop earrings, and bold red lipstick. Her hair is styled into a tight perm, and numerous golden bangle bracelets encase her wrists.

Charlene is dressed in an equally stylish animal print jumpsuit with a matching headscarf, a chunky gold necklace, red pumps, and a dramatic, bejeweled brooch affixed confidently to her lapel. Her fiery red nails add to her flair, and her mischievous smile betrays an inclination towards troublemaking.

INT. SIMMONS FAMILY KITCHEN - DAY

Lucinda is busy stirring a pot of thick gravy, while Charlene stirs a bowl of whipped cream with a wooden spoon. They are engaged in a spirited conversation. Their knees lightly brush each other's while they shift in place in a hip, syncopated motion.

LUCINDA
(in a musical tone with a smile)
Oh, Charlene, you surely got the thickest and creamiest whipped cream here! Who would have thought that adding a pinch of vanilla extract would make it taste this good?

CHARLENE
(eyes rolling, sarcastically)
Oh please, Lucy. You act like it's the first time you heard about that trick. (Pause) Although, to be honest, it seems almost too fluffy to eat. It's like you could wear it like a hat or something!

Both the women pause a beat, before looking at each other slyly, as if daring one another. They then burst into peals of laughter. After a moment, Charlene, with an exaggerated wink, dips her fingers into the bowl of whipped cream, and gently wipes it across Lucinda's forehead.

LUCINDA
(surprised, eyebrows raised and feigning indignation)
Girl, you did not just give me a whipped cream facelift!

Charlene smirks at Lucinda, while sassy undertones prevail.

CHARLENE
(grinning)
It's only fair, Lucy. Now, you have the same heavenly whipped cream scent all over, just like our desserts. And, who knows, maybe it'll help that little wrinkle, too?

Lucinda, similar to a feline with a temper, reaches for a nearby pot of gravy and, with a graceful movement, pours just a spoonful of it onto Charlene's head.

LUCINDA
(scolding)
You're asking for it, Charlene! Maybe you need a little fashion update, too - with a gravy-styled hairdo!

Charlene, shocked for a moment, regains her composure and smirks.

CHARLENE
(revengeful whisper)
You brought this upon yourself, you know.

Charlene scoops a generous portion of whipped cream with a large ladle and dramatically pours it onto Lucinda's head, covering her perfectly styled hair, and cascading down over her face.

Before Lucinda can react, she grabs Charlene's bowl of whipped cream, and both women proceed to engage in a tit-for-tat food fight, as the atmosphere shifts from being mischievous to outright dramatic. All others gasp and take a step back, forming a circle around the two combatants. A flurry of whipped cream, gravy, spaghetti, and other foods are flying through the air. The camera pans over the kitchen chaos, and we see even the covered dessert table becomes a casualty of the foody war.

INT. SIMMONS FAMILY KITCHEN - DAY

The food fight continues for a minute until both women are almost covered head-to-toe in various dishes. And before it crosses the line, Lucinda pauses and raises her hands in surrender.

LUCINDA
(out of breath, laughing)
Truce! Truce, Charlene! We've made a greater mess than if our children had done it!

CHARLENE
(panting and laughing)
You're right, you're right! But at least we didn't ruin that delicious cake you made.

Lucinda and Charlene are out of breath, shoulders heaving with laughter, while the onlookers began to laugh and clap as well. The tension that was palpable during the food fight has dissipated, and everyone has a sense of fond amusement at the scene that played out before them.

INT. SIMMONS FAMILY KITCHEN - DAY

The scene ends with Lucinda and Charlene still laughing, covered in food and smiling as they wipe the mixture of whipped cream and gravy from their eyes. The camera zooms out to reveal the kitchen in a glorious disarray, a colorful canvas splattered with food and stained with laughter.

FADE OUT

assistant_message:
Once there was a boy named Val, who, on a warm summer afternoon, found himself in the company of four lovely girls at a tea party. Val was quite timid but also quite dashing. He had poofy arched light blonde hair, a thin slender figure, and fair skin. As for his attire, he wore a turtleneck shirt, a brown mid-length coat tightly cinched at the waist with a belt, poofy pants, black gloves, high-heeled knee-high boots, and a beret.

The tea party was held in the beautiful garden outside the house of one of the girls, Emma. The other girls were named Candy, Tasha, and Juicy. They were all dressed in pretty dresses and wore high-heeled sandals. It seemed as if Val was the only boy there.

The sun was shining brightly, casting dappled shadows on the lush lawn as the girls and Val gathered around a big round table that was set with delicate china teacups and saucers, crystal glasses filled with pink lemonade, and platters piled high with delicious finger sandwiches and sweet pastries. The girls chatted and giggled while Val listened quietly, taking in the fragrant scents of the garden and the gentle sounds of tea being poured and silverware clinking.

At one point, Juicy got up from her seat to fix the strap of her sandal. Just then, the wind suddenly picked up, and with a mischievous gust, it lifted her elegant dress, exposing her pink panties for everyone to see. Her cheeks instantly flushed bright red with embarrassment, and she couldn't hold back a few tears as she hurriedly smoothed her dress down.

Val noticed Juicy's distress and immediately stood up from his seat. In a gentle and composed voice, he told her, "Please don't be so upset, Juicy. It was just an innocent accident, and the wind is to blame. You have no reason to be ashamed." He then picked up a nearby napkin and offered it to her to wipe her tears away.

The girls were astonished by Val's gentlemanly reaction. They had expected a boy in his place to make fun of Juicy or act like a pervert, but Val behaved with maturity and kindness. They looked at him with newfound admiration in their eyes, their previous laughter forgotten in the wake of his gallant actions. 

Overwhelmed by Val's compassion, Juicy looked at him with gratitude in her eyes. She quickly wiped away her tears and managed a small, grateful smile. "Thank you so much, Val. I'm truly grateful for your kindness," she whispered shyly.

The tea party continued, and a new sense of camaraderie developed around the table. Val's gentle nature won over the hearts of the girls, and they began engaging him in conversation, wanting to know more about him.

As the afternoon sun began to set and the tea party drew to an end, Val bid the girls farewell. He felt a sense of accomplishment for having faced his shyness, and he knew he had made some wonderful new friends in the process. He looked back at the beautiful garden and the lovely ladies who had been his companions that day, knowing this would be an afternoon he would never forget. And as he walked away, Emma, Candy, Tasha, and Juicy couldn't help but feel their lives had been touched, albeit in a small way, by the incredible young man named Val.

assistant_message:
If Britain had never colonized the world, the current global landscape would be radically different in various aspects, such as political boundaries, language, culture, and economic systems. Here is a detailed hypothetical breakdown of how the world might look:

1. Political boundaries: Many of today's countries could have different borders or may not even exist. The United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and various nations in Africa and the Caribbean might have different political structures and territories. In the absence of British colonization, indigenous populations might have retained control over their lands, or other European powers could have established their influence in these regions.

2. Language: English would not be the globally dominant language it is today. Instead, languages like Spanish, French, or Dutch could have gained more international prominence due to the colonial efforts of Spain, France, and the Netherlands. Additionally, local languages in various regions might have been preserved more effectively, leading to a more linguistically diverse world.

3. Culture: The spread of British culture and values across the world has largely influenced global cultural development. If Britain never colonized the world, indigenous and regional cultures might have retained a stronger influence in their respective regions, and cultural exchanges between different parts of the world would be more diverse. For example, sports like cricket and rugby might not be as popular as they are today outside the UK, and global fashion and architectural styles would be quite different.

4. Economic systems: The rise of capitalism and the industrial revolution were both closely tied to the British Empire's influence on global trade and economics. If Britain never colonized the world, mercantilism might have persisted more broadly, or other economic systems could have emerged in its place. This could result in different patterns of global trade, different dominant industries, and potentially altered rates of economic growth in various regions.

5. Scientific and technological development: The British Empire has made significant contributions to scientific and technological advancements, such as the invention of the steam engine and key contributions to modern medicine. Without British colonization, these developments might have occurred at a different pace or under different circumstances, impacting the trajectory of global scientific and technological progress.

6. International relations: The absence of the British Empire could fundamentally change the balance of power at various points in history. Without British involvement, conflicts such as the Napoleonic Wars, World Wars I and II, and countless smaller conflicts could have entirely different outcomes. This, in turn, would lead to alternative global power structures and alliances.

While it is impossible to know precisely how the world would be if Britain never colonized it, we can say that the political, linguistic, cultural, economic, and global power dynamics would be dramatically different from what they are today. The colonial legacy of Britain has left a significant impact on the course of world history, and without it, we would be living in a very different world.

Provide a design for a disk topology for a NAS built on TrueNAS Scale, as well as a dataset layout. The available disks are as follows:

- 2x 18TB disks
- 5x 14TB disks
- 3x 12TB disk
- 4x 8TB disks
- 2x 120GB disks
- 2x SLOW 8TB drives

There are 17 drive bays available. The two smallest disks are to be used for a mirrored pool that servers as a boot device. The two slow drives are SMR disks that will be used in their own pool to provide a Time Machine target for some Macs. You are asked to design the topology. The data being stored includes video files, music files, disk images, archived software, photos, and some text files. While much of the data could be recreated or downloaded, some of it is impossible to replace. You may leave bays available for a hot spare or to allow for future expansion. I prefer not to use RAIDZ, as mirrored arrays rebuild faster.

My main priorities are redundancy to reduce the risk of data loss, cost efficiency, and space efficiency. Raw performance is not a significant concern.

If you need more information before creating your design, please provide me with a short questionnaire.
assistant_message:
Design for a Disk Topology for a NAS built on TrueNAS Scale:

1. Create a mirrored boot pool using the two 120GB disks.
2. Use the two SMR 8TB drives to create a separate pool for Time Machine targets for the Macs.
3. For the remaining data, create three separate mirrored vdevs, grouping the disks based on capacity:
   - Pair the 2x 18TB disks together
   - Pair 2x 14TB disks and leave a bay available for future expansion (hot spare or additional disk)
   - Pair 2x 12TB disks and leave a bay available for future expansion (hot spare or additional disk)
   - Pair 2x 8TB disks and leave two bays available for future expansion (hot spares or additional disks)
4. Add the three mirrored vdevs (from step 3) to a single storage pool to maximize space efficiency and redundancy.
5. Within the storage pool, create datasets according to the data type, such as video files, music files, disk images, archived software, photos, and text files.

This design provides redundancy and space efficiency while making use of the available disks. Mirroring rebuild times will also be faster compared to RAIDZ. By leaving some bays available for future expansion or hot spares, the NAS can easily adapt to changing storage requirements.

One afternoon, a Sunday, a new model TFord2
 slowly came up
the hill and went past the house. The boy, who happened to see it
from the porch, ran down the steps and stood on the sidewalk. The
driver was looking right and left as if trying to find a particular ad
dress; he turned the car around at the corner and came back. Pulling
up before the boy, he idled his throttle and beckoned with a gloved
hand. He was a Negro. His car shone. The brightwork gleamed... I
am looking for a young woman of color whose name is Sarah, be said.
She is said to reside in one of these houses.
The boy realized he meant the woman in the attic. She’s here. The
man switched off the motor, set the brake and jumped down.
When Mother came to the door the colored man was respectful,
but there was something disturbingly resolute and selfimportant
in the way he asked her if he could please speak with Sarah. Mother
could not judge his age. He was a stocky man with a redcomplect
ed shining brown face, high cheekbones and large dark eyes so in
tense as to suggest they were about to cross. He had a neat mous
tache. He was dressed in the affection of wealth to which colored
people lent themselves.
She told him to wait and closed the door. She climbed to the
third floor. She found the girl Sarah not sitting at the window as
she usually did but standing rigidly, hands folded in front of her,
and facing the door. Sarah, Mother said, you have a caller. The girl
said nothing. Will you come to the kitchen? The girl shook her head.
You don’t want to see him? No, ma’am, the girl finally said softly,
while she looked at the floor. Send him away, please. This was the
most she had said in all the months she had lived in the house. Moth
er went back downstairs and found the fellow not at the back door
but in the kitchen where, in the warmth of the comer near the cook
stove, Sarah’s baby lay sleeping in his carriage. The black man was
kneeling beside the carriage and staring at the child. Mother, not
thinking clearly, was suddenly outraged that he had presumed to
come in the door. Sarah is unable to see you, she said and she held
the door open. The colored man took another glance at the child,
rose, thanked her and departed.
Such was the coming of the colored man in the car to Broad
view Avenue. His name was Coalhouse Walker Jr. Beginning with
that Sunday he appeared every week, always knocking at the back
door. Always turning away without complaint upon Sarah’s re
fusal to see him. Father considered the visits a nuisance and want
ed to discourage them. I’ll call the police, he said. Mother laid her
hand on his arm. One Sunday the colored man left a bouquet of
yellow chrysanthemums which in this season had to have cost him
a pretty penny.
The black girl would say nothing about her visitor. They had no
idea where she had met him, or how. As far as they knew she had no
family nor any friends from the black community in the downtown
section of the city. Apparently she had come by herself from New
York to work as a servant. Mother was exhilarated by the situation.
She began to regret Sarah’s intransigence. She thought of the drive
from Harlem, where Coalhouse Walker Jr. lived, and the drive back,
and she decided the next time to give him more of a visit. She would
serve tea in the parlor. Father questioned the propriety of this.
Mother said, he is wellspoken and conducts himself as a gentle
man. I see nothing wrong with it. When Mr Roosevelt3
 was in the
White House he gave dinner to Booker T. Washington. Surely we
can serve tea to Coalhouse Walker Jr.
And so it happened on the next Sunday that the Negro took tea.
Father noted that he suffered no embarrassment by being in the parlor with a cup and saucer in his hand. On the contrary, he acted as if it
was the most natural thing in the world. The surroundings did not
awe him nor was his manner deferential. He was courteous and cor
rect. He told them about himself. He was a professional pianist and
was now more or less permanently located in New York, having se
cured a job with the Jim Europe Clef Club Orchestra, a wellknown
ensemble that gave regular concerts at the Manhattan4
 Casino on 155th Street and Eighth Avenue. It was important, he said, for a musician to find a place that was permanent, a job that required no travelling... I am through travelling, he said. I am through going on the
road. He spoke so fervently that Father realized the message was in
tended for the woman upstairs. This irritated him. What can you play?
he said abruptly. Why don’t you play something for us?
The black man placed tea on the tray. He rose, patted his lips with
the napkin, placed the napkin beside his cup and went to the piano.
He sat on the piano stool and immediately rose and twirled it till the
height was to his satisfaction. He sat down again, played a chord and
turned to them. This piano is badly in need of a tuning, he said. Fa
ther’s face reddened. Oh, yes. Mother said, we are terrible about that.
The musician turned again to the keyboard. “Wall Street5
 Rag,” he
said. Composed by the great Scott Joplin.6
 He began to play. Illtunedor not the Aeolian had never made such sounds. Small clear chords
hung in the air like flowers. The melodies were like bouquets. There
seemed to be no other possibilities for life than those delineated by
the music. When the piece was over Coalhouse Walker turned on the
stool and found in his audience the entire family: Mother, Father, the
boy, Grandfather and Mother’s Younger Brother, who had come down
from his room in shirt and suspenders to see who was playing. Of all
of them he was the only one who knew ragtime. He had heard it in his
nightlife period in New York. He had never expected to hear it in his
sister’s home.
Coalhouse Walker Jr. turned back to the piano and said “The
Maple Leaf”. Composed by the great Scott Joplin. The most famous
rag of all rang through the air. The pianist sat stiffly at the key
board, his long dark hands with their pink nails seemingly with no
effort producing the clusters of syncopating chords and the thump
ing octaves. This was a most robust composition, a vigorous music
that roused the senses and never stood still a moment. The boy per
ceived it as light touching various places in space, accumulating in
intricate patterns until the entire room was made to glow with its
own being. The music filled the stairwell to the third floor where the mute and unforgiving Sarah sat with her hands folded and lis
tened with the door open.
The piece was brought to a conclusion. Everyone applauded. Moth
er then introduced Mr Walker to Grandfather and to Younger Brother,
who shook the black man’s hand and said I am pleased to meet you.
Coalhouse Walker was solemn. Everyone was standing. There was a
silence. Father cleared his throat. Father was not knowledgeable in
music. His taste ran to Carrie Jacobs Bond.7
 He thought Negro music
had to have smiling and cakewalkmg. Do you know any coon songs?8
he said. He did not intend to be rude — coon songs was what they
were called. But the pianist responded with a tense shake of the head.
Coon songs are made for minstrel shows,9
 he said. White men sing
them in blackface. There was another silence. The black man looked
at the ceiling. Well, he said, it appears as if Miss Sarah will not be able
to receive me. He turned abruptly and walked through the hall to the
kitchen. The family followed him. He had left his coat on a chair. He
put it on and ignoring them all, he knelt and gazed at the baby asleep
in its carriage. After several moments he stood up, said good day and
walked out of the door.

5. An optimistic view of the future: The Star Trek universe presents a hopeful vision of humanity's future, with humanity having overcome many contemporary issues like poverty, war, disease, and prejudice.

The primary objective of this project was to create a genomic library using a streptomycinresistant strain of E.coli Top10 (4537 bp) as the genomic DNA, incorporating it into a pUC19
plasmid (2686 bp) vector (Cirino et al., 2003). The successful construction of this genomic
library was expected to confer streptomycin resistance to a recipient E.coli strain Mach1
through the functional selection of the rspL gene (Hanahan, 1983). However, throughout the
experiment, several challenges were encountered, leading to changes in the experimental
design and troubleshooting of errors.
An initial gel electrophoresis performed to confirm the presence of the rspL gene after digestion
of genomic DNA with BamHI resulted in no visible bands. This was primarily due to the low
concentration of the originally isolated genomic Top10 DNA (33.2 ng/µL), which was further
diluted during the digestion reaction and loading of the gel (Inoue et al., 1990). This
concentration was below the minimum detection limit required for the INtRON RedSafeTM
nucleic acid stain to work efficiently (50 ng/µL). As a consequence, no bands were detected,
and the experiment had to be repeated with a new and cleaned up genomic DNA sample.
Subsequent gel electrophoresis performed after digesting the cleaned-up genomic DNA with
BamHI showed successful digestion of the genomic Top10 DNA, as evidenced by a shorter
smear in comparison to the uncut band of the genomic DNA (Sorek et al., 2013). In addition, the
plasmid pUC19 showed two very faint bands after digestion with BamHI, indicating appropriate
digestion of the plasmid as well.

plasmid pUC19 (vector) (Chen & Dubnau, 2004). After overnight incubation at 4 °C, the ligated
product was transformed into Mach1 chemically competent cells. The initial transformation
results were inconclusive due to contamination observed in the positive control plate.
Moreover, the second transformation attempt resulted in an unsuccessful transformation due
to inefficient uptake of DNA by the host organism, which might have been caused by several
factors, such as improper preparation of competent cells, issues concerning the ligation
reaction, or the transformation protocol itself (Inoue et al., 1990).
To increase the likelihood of obtaining a fragment containing the rspL gene, a third gel
electrophoresis was performed using HindIII in addition to BamHI for digesting both genomic
Top10 DNA and plasmid pUC19 (Cirino et al., 2003). The use of two different enzymes would
increase the accuracy of the construct and facilitate the incorporation of the desired fragment
into the plasmid (Hanahan, 1983).
Based on the information provided by the restriction analyzer, the BamHI enzyme cuts at two
different sites on genomic DNA (180 and 2865), producing large fragments that appeared as a
smear in the gel electrophoresis images (Sorek et al., 2013). HindIII was introduced to cut at an
additional site (4130) on genomic DNA, increasing the likelihood that the fragment containing
the rspL gene would be successfully incorporated into the plasmid (Chen & Dubnau, 2004).
In summary, the construction of a genomic library using E.coli Top10 genomic DNA and pUC19
plasmid DNA encountered several challenges throughout the experiment, including low DNA
concentrations, contamination, and inefficient transformation (Inoue et al., 1990). The
introduction of the HindIII enzyme in addition to BamHI for restriction digestion was expected
to increase the probability of obtaining a fragment containing the rspL gene (Cirino et al., 2003).
Furthermore, troubleshooting in each area of competent cells preparation, ligation reaction,
and transformation protocol can assist in identifying and rectifying these challenges, such as reevaluating the insert-to-vector ratio, incubation time, and temperature for the ligation reaction
or testing and optimizing various transformation conditions (Hanahan, 1983).
For this experiment, the most likely problem would be with transformation. It could be
optimized and modified by making changes mentioned below:
a. Temperature and duration: Confirm that the heat shock conditions (e.g. 42°C for 30-45
seconds) are appropriate for your cells (Inoue et al., 1990).
b. Recovery duration: Allow adequate time (usually 1 hour) for the cells to recover and express
the antibiotic resistance marker (Sorek et al., 2013).
c. Optimal antibiotic concentration: Ensure the appropriate concentration of streptomycin for
selection is used on the plates. Too high or low of a concentration may result in inadequate
selection (Chen & Dubnau, 2004).
Part B write up 16
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
In addition to the technical challenges faced during the genomic library construction, human
errors could also have contributed to the unsuccessful or inconclusive results. These errors can
occur in sample handling, reagent preparation, equipment usage, and protocol execution. Such
errors may include:
1. Cross-contamination: During handling of samples, there is potential for cross-contamination
between different DNA samples or between the samples and reagents, leading to undesired
results (Inoue et al., 1990).
2. Reagent preparation: Errors can occur while preparing various reagents such as buffers,
enzyme solutions, or antibiotics. These could include inaccurate measurement or mixing of
components, resulting in incorrect concentrations that can affect experimental outcomes
(Sorek et al., 2013).
3. Pipetting errors: Inaccurate pipetting can lead to incorrect volumes being dispensed, resulting
in the incorrect sample or reagent concentration, which affects the outcome of experiments
(Hanahan, 1983).
4. Equipment usage: Improper operation, maintenance, or calibration of laboratory equipment
can generate unreliable or inconsistent results. For instance, inaccurate temperature settings
for incubation or heat shock can affect the transformation efficiency (Chen & Dubnau, 2004).
To minimize human errors, it is essential to maintain good laboratory practices, maintaining
proper organization of the workspace, labeling samples accurately, and double-checking
reagent concentrations. Additionally, regularly calibrating and maintaining equipment,
following established protocols carefully, and incorporating appropriate controls into
experiments will help reduce the occurrence of human errors and enhance the overall success
of the genomic library construction process.
Future experiments can investigate alternative restriction enzymes, plasmid vectors, and
competent cell strains to improve the overall success of the genomic library construction
process (Cirino et al., 2003). Moreover, ensuring a suitable recovery time for transformed cells,
providing a nutrient-rich medium during recovery, using appropriate plating methods and
conditions, and including positive and negative controls in each transformation experiment will
aid in enhancing the efficiency of the genomic library construction and subsequent functional
selection of the streptomycin resistance-conferring rspL gene (Hanahan, 1983).

assistant_message:
这个错误通常是由于尝试使用一个超出了DataFrame列数或行数范围的位置进行索引引起的。

最可能的原因是你尝试使用非法的行或列索引进行了数据选择或操作。你需要检查你的代码，找出超出DataFrame范围的位置，并进行修正。

这里提供一个常见的错误示例，可能会导致上述错误。例如，当DataFrame中只有一列数据时，尝试使用iloc函数获取第二列数据会触发IndexError:

```python
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_excel('example.xlsx', usecols=[0])
data = df.iloc[:,1] # IndexError: single positional indexer is out-of-bounds
```

上述代码中，使用read_excel函数读取Excel文件，只选择第一列数据。但是在获取数据时，代码错误地将列索引指定为1，这将导致IndexError异常。正确的列索引应该是0。

如果你的错误场景与此不同，可以根据错误提示信息和代码具体情况来确定错误原因，进一步进行调试。

Economic activity is typically measured using a variety of indicators, including:

1. Gross Domestic Product (GDP): This is the most common measure of economic activity, and it represents the total value of all goods and services produced in a country over a given period of time, usually a year.

2. Gross National Product (GNP): This measure takes into account all the goods and services produced by a country's citizens, no matter where they are produced.

3. Employment and Unemployment rates: These measures indicate the number of people who are employed and those who are looking for work, which provides insights into the health of the labor market.

4. Consumer Price Index (CPI): This measure tracks the changes in the prices of goods and services over time, which reflects the rate of inflation.

5. Industrial output: This is the measure of the total production in the industrial and manufacturing sectors.

6. Trade balance: This measure tracks the difference between the value of a country's exports and imports.

7. Retail sales: This measure reflects the total sales by retailers and is an indicator of consumer spending.

assistant_message:
Decompyle++ (pycdc) is a decompiler that can help you translate Python bytecode (usually stored in .pyc files) back into the regular Python source code. Here's how to use it:

Step 1: Install Decompyle++

Before you can use Decompyle++, you'll need to install it on your system. You can clone the decompiler from the GitHub repository:

```
$ git clone https://github.com/zrax/pycdc.git
```

Step 2: Build Decompyle++

Next, you need to build pycdc. Navigate to the pycdc folder and run the following commands:

```
$ cd pycdc
$ cmake .
$ make
```

Step 3: Get the bytecode file

You should have a .pyc file, which contains the Python bytecode that you want to translate back to regular Python code. If you don't have the .pyc file, you can generate one using the Python built-in `compile()` function:

```python
import py_compile
py_compile.compile('path_to_your_python_file.py')
```

This will generate a .pyc file in a __pycache__ folder located in the same directory as the .py file.

Step 4: Run Decompyle++ to translate bytecode

Once you have the .pyc file, you can run Decompyle++ on it to get the regular Python code. From the pycdc folder, run:

```
$ ./pycdc path_to_your_bytecode_file.pyc > output.py
```

This command will decompile the bytecode in the .pyc file and save the result into the output.py file.

Now you should have the output.py file that contains the translated Python code from the bytecode.

Keep in mind that decompiled code may not be exactly the same as the original source code. Variable names or comments may be different or missing, and some code structures could be modified. However, Decompyle++ does a reasonably good job of reconstructing the original source code in most cases.

user_message: In a hypothetical application, a program must calculate the divergence of a centerline of  slip-road diverging from a main carrigeway with a fixed radius.   For a given distance d from the start of the divergence , write a program to calculate the offset of the center line of the slip-road from the main carrigeway, and the angle formed between the slip road and the main carrigeway at that point. Output those values to the console. Use any appropriate general programming language
assistant_message:
Here's one possible solution in Python:

```python
import math

# Constants
RADIUS = 100  # radius of the curve
LANE_WIDTH = 3.5  # width of each lane
SHOULDER_WIDTH = 1.5  # width of the shoulder (if any)
RAD_TO_DEG = 180 / math.pi  # conversion factor from radians to degrees

# Inputs
d = 50  # distance from start of divergence

# Calculations
alpha = math.atan2(d, RADIUS)  # angle between tangent and radius at d
theta = math.asin((LANE_WIDTH + SHOULDER_WIDTH) / (2 * RADIUS))  # half angle between lanes
beta = alpha - theta  # angle between tangent and lane centerline
offset = RADIUS * math.tan(beta) - LANE_WIDTH / 2  # offset of centerline from main carriageway

# Output
print("At distance d =", d, "from start of divergence:")
print("Offset from main carriageway:", offset, "meters")
print("Angle between slip road and main carriageway:", beta * RAD_TO_DEG, "degrees")
```

This program uses the `math` library to perform the necessary trigonometric calculations. It assumes that the slip road and main carriageway are both straight before and after the diverging curve, and that the lanes and shoulder are of equal width throughout. Alice and Bob share binary communication channel C. 

The channel C is faulty in that it drops a bit (ie, a package) with probability 1-p. 

If one party sends a bit b through the channel, then the other party receives the bit b with probability p = 0.9, and  receives no bit with probability 1-p = 0.1.

Alice sends 3 bits through the channel C to Bob. 

What is the probability that Bob receives at least 2 bits?
assistant_message:
We can solve this by finding the probabilities of the different scenarios where Bob receives at least 2 bits and then summing up those probabilities.

Let X_i be the event that the i-th bit is received by Bob, for i = 1, 2, 3.

We need to find the probability of these three scenarios:
1. Bob receives all three bits (X_1, X_2, and X_3): P(X_1)P(X_2)P(X_3)
2. Bob receives only the first two bits (X_1 and X_2, but not X_3): P(X_1)P(X_2)(1-P(X_3))
3. Bob receives only the first and third bits (X_1 and X_3, but not X_2): P(X_1)(1-P(X_2))P(X_3)
4. Bob receives only the second and third bits (X_2 and X_3, but not X_1): (1-P(X_1))P(X_2)P(X_3)

Since each bit is received with probability p = 0.9:

1. P(X_1)P(X_2)P(X_3) = (0.9)(0.9)(0.9) = 0.9^3 = 0.729
2. P(X_1)P(X_2)(1-P(X_3)) = (0.9)(0.9)(1-0.9) = 0.9^2(0.1) = 0.081 
3. P(X_1)(1-P(X_2))P(X_3) = (0.9)(1-0.9)(0.9) = 0.9^2(0.1) = 0.081
4. (1-P(X_1))P(X_2)P(X_3) = (1-0.9)(0.9)(0.9) = 0.9^2(0.1) = 0.081

Now, we sum up the probabilities of these four scenarios:

P(Bob receives at least 2 bits) = 0.729 + 0.081 + 0.081 + 0.081 = 0.972

So, the probability that Bob receives at least 2 bits is 0.972.

If I'm tapping on these numbers as randomly as possible with 3 fingers at a rate of 6 taps per second, how long would it take for me to correctly tap a sequence of four random numbers?
assistant_message:
The total number of possible sequences of four numbers that can be tapped in the grid is (9 x 9 x 9 x 9) - 1 (since 0 cannot be part of the sequence) = 65,536.

The probability of tapping any one specific sequence is 1/65,536.

The probability of tapping the correct sequence on any given set of 4 taps is also 1/65,536, since you are tapping randomly.

The probability of NOT tapping the correct sequence on any given set of 4 taps is therefore 1 - 1/65,536 = 65,535/65,536.

The probability of NOT tapping the correct sequence on any given set of 4 taps for N sets of 4 taps is (65,535/65,536)^N.

So, the probability of tapping the correct sequence in N sets of 4 taps is 1 - (65,535/65,536)^N.

We want to find the value of N such that this probability is greater than or equal to 0.5 (i.e., a 50% chance of correctly tapping the sequence).

1 - (65,535/65,536)^N >= 0.5

(65,535/65,536)^N <= 0.5

N * log(65,535/65,536) <= log(0.5)

N >= log(0.5) / log(65,535/65,536)

Using a calculator, N is approximately 37,441.

Therefore, it would take approximately (37,441 x 4) / 6 = 24,960.67 seconds or 416.01 minutes or 6.93 hours to correctly tap a sequence of four random numbers.

Summary
Language models can speed up and automate many tasks in areas such as text or code. What happens when they run themselves?

This new trend in generative AI is also called “self-prompting” or “auto-prompting”. The language model develops and executes prompts that can lead to new prompts based on an initial input.

This approach becomes truly powerful when combined with tools such as web search or the ability to test written code. The language model becomes an automatic assistant that can do much more than just generate text or code.

“1 GPT call is a bit like 1 thought. Stringing them together in loops creates agents that can perceive, think, and act, their goals defined in English in prompts,” writes OpenAI developer Andrej Karpathy, predicting a future of “AutoOrgs” made up of “AutoCEOs,” “AutoCFOs,” and so on.

Ad

Auto-GPT: Self-Prompting is the latest trend in large language models
The most popular self-prompting example at the moment is the experimental open source application “Auto-GPT”. According to the Github team, the Python application is designed to independently develop and manage business ideas and generate income.

The program plans step-by-step, justifies decisions and develops plans, which it documents. In addition to integrating GPT-4 for text generation, the system has Internet access for data retrieval, can store data, and can generate speech via the Elevenlabs API. Supposedly, the system is even capable of self-improvement and bug-fixing by generating Python scripts via GPT-4.

The idea behind Auto-GPT and similar projects like Baby-AGI or Jarvis (HuggingGPT) is to network language models and functions to automate complex tasks. “By leveraging the strong language capability of ChatGPT and abundant AI models in Hugging Face, HuggingGPT is able to cover numerous sophisticated AI tasks in different modalities and domains and achieve impressive results in language, vision, speech, and other challenging tasks, which paves a new way towards advanced artificial intelligence,” writes the team behind HuggingGPT.

Language models as a platform
The idea of using language models to go beyond pure text generation is not new: The startup Adept is working on a universal text control system that allows a language model agent to search a website, research Wikipedia, or operate Excel using only language. The present study, therefore, aims to investigate the physiological and behavioral factors that significantly impact older adults' thermal comfort perception and adaptability, drawing on a systematic review of existing literature in the field.

As older adults physiologically experience changes in their thermoregulatory systems, manifesting as altered temperature perception, decreased capacity to dissipate heat, and diminished vascular response to cold, it is essential to consider these physiological variations when developing thermal comfort guidelines. Moreover, research has shown that age-related physiological changes such as decreased metabolic rate, reduced muscle mass, altered blood flow, and decreased sweat production contribute to differences in thermoregulatory response, thereby influencing individual preferences for ambient temperature and air movement. For instance, decreased vasodilation and vasoconstriction capabilities can impede the body's ability to maintain optimal thermal balance, rendering older adults more vulnerable to temperature fluctuations outside their comfort zone. Furthermore, altered perception of thermal discomfort due to age-related sensory impairments could also make it challenging for older individuals to communicate or recognize their personal thermal preferences accurately.

Behavioral factors, such as clothing preferences and activity levels, can also play a crucial role in determining thermal comfort and adaptive capacity among older occupants. In addition, activity patterns shift in later life stages, with sedentary activities becoming more prevalent, leading to a decrease in internal heat production, ultimately affecting the preferred temperature range. Therefore, attention must be paid to these changes in preference and activity to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the factors affecting thermal comfort for older occupants.

To address these physiological and behavioral considerations, a multi-faceted approach to thermal comfort optimization is required. The outcomes of this research contribute to the identification of critical parameters for building design that can effectively address the thermal comfort challenges faced by older adults, with potential ramifications on their overall well-being, health, and quality of life. Findings from the systematic review aid in synthesizing a set of design guidelines and strategies that can inform architects, designers, and urban planners on creating inclusive, sustainable living spaces for the growing older population. These age-inclusive building design approaches, when implemented, provide a significant contribution to the broader objective of promoting age-friendly communities that accommodate the diverse needs of older occupants and enhance their quality of life in the long term.

In conclusion, the identification of physiological and behavioral factors affecting thermal comfort perception and adaptability in older adults is essential for shaping age-inclusive building design strategies. 1. Hyperbole: Use exaggerated language to emphasize your symptoms. For example, "I feel like I'm dying."

2. Metaphor: Compare your symptoms to something else to emphasize their severity. For example, "My body is a furnace, burning up with fever."

3. Anaphora: Repeat key phrases to emphasize your symptoms. For example, "My head is pounding, my throat is sore, and my nose won't stop running."

4. Euphemism: Use a mild or indirect term to describe something unpleasant. For example, "I've got a bit of a bug."

5. Irony: Use sarcasm to emphasize your symptoms. For example, "Oh, I'm just loving this constant cough and headache."

6. Ellipsis: Use pauses or incomplete sentences to emphasize your symptoms. For example, "I can barely breathe...throat feels like sandpaper...eyes raw from sneezing...pray for me."

7. Pathos: Appeal to the reader's emotions by describing how miserable you feel. For example, "I feel so terrible, I haven't been able to sleep or eat anything all day."

8. Simile: Use a comparison to emphasize your symptoms. For example, "My stomach is in knots like a bunched up sheet."

9. Alliteration: Repeat consonant sounds for emphasis. For example, "My head is throbbing and my nose is running rivers."

10. Personification: Give human characteristics to your symptoms. For example, "This fever is relentless, it's like a monster that won't let me rest."

user_message: how is the distinction between intermediate and final goods important for calculating gdp of a nation
assistant_message:
The distinction between intermediate and final goods is important in calculating the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a nation since only the final goods are included in GDP. The production of intermediate goods is already accounted for in the final goods that are produced using those intermediate goods. Thus, if the intermediate goods were included in GDP, it would lead to double-counting.

To avoid double-counting, only the value of the final goods and services that are consumed in the economy are included in GDP. For instance, if a car company produces 1000 cars and sells them to a dealership for $30,000 each, the total value of production will be $30 million ($30,000 x 1000). However, when calculating GDP, only the value of the cars sold to the final customers should be included, not the value of cars sold to dealerships. This is because cars sold to dealerships are treated as intermediate goods and will be used to produce final goods.

Therefore, the distinction between intermediate and final goods is important in calculating GDP as it helps in avoiding the risk of double-counting and provides a more accurate estimation of the value of goods and services produced in a country over time.

Aemilia and Caelius sat Celestria down in their cozy living room, a warm hearth fire crackling as they prepared to discuss the significance of the Sovereign’s Chalice that now hung from her collar.

Background
This portion of the lab section involved creating a genomic library using a streptomycin
resistant strain of E.coli top10 (4537 bp) as the genomic DNA which will be incorporated into
puc19 plasmid (2686 bp) vector as proposed earlier in PART B proposal document.
To achieve the proposed plan, E.coli strain top10 (4537 bp) will serve as the genomic strain that
will be the source of streptomycin resistance rspL gene. The FastDigest HindIII (thermo
scientific) digested fragment will be insert into a digested pUC19 plasmid vector (2686 bp)
utilizing ligation process. Once ligated, the product will be transformed with Mach1 chemically
competent cells (O.D. value = 0.77). To confirm the success of ligation the transformed product
will be plated on Ampillicin/X-gal/IPTG plates and the white colonies will then be streaked onto
streptomycin plates to verify the rspl gene streptomycin resistance property.
As per the proposal, digesting the bacterial strains with similar digestion enzyme (HindIII) prior
to ligation followed by transformation would have ideally given the genomic library however,
throughout the project certain decisions were changed based on the results which will be
thoroughly covered in this document along with the solutions taken to troubleshoot the
mistakes.
Methods/Materials
Isolation of genomic DNA and plasmid DNA:
To start with the procedure of creating a genomic library from E.coli strain Top10 and plasmid
pUC19, 5 mL genomic DNA (Top10) and 3 mL plasmid pUC19 was isolated using GeneJET
genomic DNA purification kit (lot 01319594) and GeneJET plasmid Mini prep kit (lot 01218820)
respectively.
Table 1: Observed concentrations of isolated genomic material using SimpliNano.
Genomic material A260/A280 A260/A230 DNA Conc. (ng/µL)
Top10 1.988 1.644 33.2
pUC19 1.866 1.211 17.2
The above table summarizes the observed concentration data for isolated genomic material on
Feb 21, 2023. The volume of sample loaded in SimpliNano was 2 µL for both DNA. Elution
buffer(01177350 and 00991597) from both respective isolation kits were used as a blank on
SimpliNano.
Part B write up 2
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
Restriction Enzyme Digestion:
As per part A proposal our group wanted to use HindIII enzyme of restriction enzyme digestion
but BamHI was used instead. This was changed because the aim was to check whether BamHI
will show same digestion or similar results with strainTop10 of E.coli as it was the case with K12
strain.
Both genomic DNA from Top10 and plasmid DNA of pUC19 were digested with thermos
scientific FastDigest BamHI enzyme in second week of this project (March 8, 2023) and the
reagent volumes used are listed in the table given below.
Table 2: Reagents for restriction enzyme digestion of genomic material.
Digestion Reagents pUC19 Top10 (rspL gene)
Genetic material 2 µL 10 µL
Fast digest buffer 2 µL 2 µL
BamHI (Fast Digest Enzyme) 1 µL 1 µL
PCR Grade Water 30 µL 22 µL
Total Reaction volume 35 µL 35 µL
This table summarizes the reagent recipe used for first restriction enzyme digestion of genetic
materials used to create the genomic library. The above listed both digestion reactions were
incubated in 37 °C water bath for 30 minutes before heat inactivation at 80 °C for 10 minutes.
Gel electrophoresis to verify digestion from band sizes:
This gel electrophoresis was performed on same day in order to confirm whether the digestion
was successful or not and whether the isolated genomic DNA contains the rspL gene. To
prepare this, 1% gel was prepared using 500 mg BIOTECHNOLOGY GRADE Agarose ITM powder
(Lot : 19H2056197) in 50 mL 1X TAE buffer with 2.5 µL INtRON RedSafeTM (0008-090501.52) for
visualization.
1Kb DNA ladder RTU (Froggo-BIO, BIO-HELIX LOT 14007210104) was used as a standard with
Thermo Scientific 6X loading dye (LOT 00799325). 10 µL of digested genomic was loaded into
the gel. Gel was run for 20 minutes at 120V. When analyzed under UV light(Midi Blue LED
Transilluminator), there were no bands visible.
DNA clean-up:
Since gel electrophoresis results indicated no bands it was decided with the help of lab
instructor to perform a DNA clean up for genomic to concentrate it more.
Originally isolated genomic Top10 DNA was cleaned up using “Thermo Scientific GeneJET Gel
Extraction and DNA clean up kit” the following week ( March 14, 2023). A small change was
introduced in original clean up protocol which stated “10 µL of Elution buffer” to elute which
Part B write up 3
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
was updated to “15 µL of Elution Buffer”. Concentration of genomic DNA was checked on
SimpliNano after clean up which indicated the DNA was lost in clean up process.
Table 3: Concentration of genomic DNA (Top10) analyzed on SimpliNano after DNA clean up.
Cleaned up genomic Top10 DNA
A260/A230 0.826
A260/A280 1.609
ng/ µL 12
The above table lists the concentration of originally isolated genomic DNA of strain Top10 after
clean-up using Thermo Scientific GeneJET Gel Extraction and DNA clean up kit (LOT 2599306).
Volume of sample loaded on SimpliNano was 2 µL and the blank used was the elution
buffer(LOT 01307087) from the DNA clean up kit.
New isolated genomic Top10 DNA provided by Vanessa:
Since the whole genomic DNA was lost therefore another vial of isolated genomic was provided
by lab instructor. The concentration of new genomic DNA was analyzed on SimpliNano which
was then cleaned-up using the same clean up kit with same modification of 15 µL elution
buffer. After clean up the concentration was checked on SimpliNano and is stated in table
below.
Table 4: Concentration of new genomic Top10 DNA before and after clean-up.
Before clean up After clean up
A260/A280 1.598 1.794
A260/A230 1.143 2.188
ng/ µL 28.1 109.6
The above table summarizes the observed concentrations of new isolated genomic top10 DNA
provided by Vanessa. These concentrations refer to the DNA before using GeneJET genomic
DNA purification kit with its corresponding elution buffer as blank. Also after clean up using
Thermo Scientific GeneJET Gel Extraction and DNA clean up kit (LOT 2599306). Volume of
sample loaded on SimpliNano was 2 µL and the blank used was the elution buffer(LOT
01307087) from the DNA clean up kit.
New Digestion reaction set up with cleaned up genomic DNA:
The new digestion was performed using the cleaned up genomic DNA with higher
concentration. The table summarizes the reaction reagents and volumes.
Table 5: The reaction reagents for restriction enzyme digestion of both genomic material.
pUC19 Top10 genomic DNA
Concentration 17.2 ng/ µL 109.6 ng/ µL
Genomic material 4 µL 5 µL
Fast Digest Buffer 2 µL 2 µL
Part B write up 4
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
Fast Digest Enzyme (BamHI) 1 µL 1 µL
PCR Grade water 28 µL 27 µL
Total reaction volume 35 µL 35 µL
The table gives the reaction volumes that were used to perform enzyme digestion of both
genetic materials used in this project to construct a genomic library. Both reactions were
incubated for half an hour in 37 °C water bath prior to heat inactivation at 80 °C for 10 minutes.
The digestion reactions were then stored in ice bucket until gel electrophoresis apparatus was
ready.
Another 1% gel electrophoresis:
Similar recipe of 1% gel electrophoresis was prepared using same supplies however since the
concentration of newly cleaned genomic DNA was significantly high, only 5 µL of cut and uncut
genomic along with cut plasmid with 6X loading dye was loaded.
The 1% gel was shared with another group with ladder in the center followed by uncut
genomic, cut genomic and cut plasmid from our samples. First half of the gel was utilized by
Mahan’s group. The gel was run for about 20-25 minutes at 120 V and the results were first
visualized under UV light (Midi Blue LED Transilluminator) and then under BIOrad software
which will be added in result section.
Ligation with only one reaction:
This was decided to check if the ligation was successful or not which was performed the
following week (March 21, 2023). To do so, a 1:1 ratio of cut plasmid pUC19 and cut genomic
top10 (insert) was ligated using T4 ligase (vector) accompanied with the use of PEG4000.
The following table summarizes the reaction reagents and volumes.
Table 6: Ligation reaction set up for digested insert and vector using T4 ligase.
Reaction reagents Ligation ratio (1:1)
Insert (digested genomic top10 DNA) 3 µL
Vector (digested pUC19) 3 µL
T4 Ligase Buffer (5X) 5 µL
T4 Ligase 2 µL
PEG4000 2 µL
PCR Grade water 10 µL
Total reaction volume 25 µL
This ligation reagent recipe was used to ligate the insert and vector achieved from restriction
enzyme digestion of genomic top10 and pUC19 with BamHI. This ligation reaction was
incubated overnight at 4 °C and heat inactivated after 24 hours at 65 °C for 10 minutes. The
ligated product was then stored at -20 °C until transformation.
Transformation with Mach 01 strain competent cells:
Part B write up 5
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
Transformation of the ligated product was performed the same week (March 24, 2023). To
proceed with transformation, 4 vials of competent cells (50 µL each) were provided by Vanessa
along with 4 agar plates.
Goal was to plate one positive control, one negative control for validation of results with one
experimental in duplicates. Protocol of transformation was used to first thaw the competent
cells on ice (about 20 minutes) followed by setting up controls and experimental.
Table 7: Controls and experimental reaction set for transformation of ligated product.
Reaction Positive control Negative control Experimental
Reagents 50 µL competent
cells + 10 µL pUC19

cells

The transformation reactions were then incubated on ice for 30 minutes prior to heat shock at
42 °C for 30 seconds. The reactions were then placed on shaker for 1 hour until recovered.
Meanwhile, when 30 minutes were left while cells were recovering, 4 agar plates were spread
with 100 µL of 25 mg/mL Ampicillin, 40 µL of 20 mg/mL X-gal and 8 µL of 500 mM IPTG per
plate respectively. After successive completion of 1 hour recovery of cells, one little change was

Discussion
The primary objective of this project was to create a genomic library using a streptomycinresistant strain of E.coli Top10 (4537 bp) as the genomic DNA, incorporating it into a pUC19
plasmid (2686 bp) vector (Cirino et al., 2003). The successful construction of this genomic
library was expected to confer streptomycin resistance to a recipient E.coli strain Mach1
through the functional selection of the rspL gene (Hanahan, 1983). However, throughout the
experiment, several challenges were encountered, leading to changes in the experimental
design and troubleshooting of errors.
An initial gel electrophoresis performed to confirm the presence of the rspL gene after digestion
of genomic DNA with BamHI resulted in no visible bands. This was primarily due to the low
concentration of the originally isolated genomic Top10 DNA (33.2 ng/µL), which was further
diluted during the digestion reaction and loading of the gel (Inoue et al., 1990). This
concentration was below the minimum detection limit required for the INtRON RedSafeTM
nucleic acid stain to work efficiently (50 ng/µL). As a consequence, no bands were detected,
and the experiment had to be repeated with a new and cleaned up genomic DNA sample.
Subsequent gel electrophoresis performed after digesting the cleaned-up genomic DNA with
BamHI showed successful digestion of the genomic Top10 DNA, as evidenced by a shorter
smear in comparison to the uncut band of the genomic DNA (Sorek et al., 2013). In addition, the
plasmid pUC19 showed two very faint bands after digestion with BamHI, indicating appropriate
digestion of the plasmid as well.
Part B write up 15
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
A ligation reaction was set up using a 1:1 ratio for cut genomic Top10 DNA (insert) and cut
plasmid pUC19 (vector) (Chen & Dubnau, 2004). After overnight incubation at 4 °C, the ligated
product was transformed into Mach1 chemically competent cells. The initial transformation
results were inconclusive due to contamination observed in the positive control plate.
Moreover, the second transformation attempt resulted in an unsuccessful transformation due
to inefficient uptake of DNA by the host organism, which might have been caused by several
factors, such as improper preparation of competent cells, issues concerning the ligation
reaction, or the transformation protocol itself (Inoue et al., 1990).
To increase the likelihood of obtaining a fragment containing the rspL gene, a third gel
electrophoresis was performed using HindIII in addition to BamHI for digesting both genomic
Top10 DNA and plasmid pUC19 (Cirino et al., 2003). The use of two different enzymes would
increase the accuracy of the construct and facilitate the incorporation of the desired fragment
into the plasmid (Hanahan, 1983).
Based on the information provided by the restriction analyzer, the BamHI enzyme cuts at two
different sites on genomic DNA (180 and 2865), producing large fragments that appeared as a
smear in the gel electrophoresis images (Sorek et al., 2013). HindIII was introduced to cut at an
additional site (4130) on genomic DNA, increasing the likelihood that the fragment containing
the rspL gene would be successfully incorporated into the plasmid (Chen & Dubnau, 2004).
In summary, the construction of a genomic library using E.coli Top10 genomic DNA and pUC19
plasmid DNA encountered several challenges throughout the experiment, including low DNA
concentrations, contamination, and inefficient transformation (Inoue et al., 1990). The
introduction of the HindIII enzyme in addition to BamHI for restriction digestion was expected
to increase the probability of obtaining a fragment containing the rspL gene (Cirino et al., 2003).
Furthermore, troubleshooting in each area of competent cells preparation, ligation reaction,
and transformation protocol can assist in identifying and rectifying these challenges, such as reevaluating the insert-to-vector ratio, incubation time, and temperature for the ligation reaction
or testing and optimizing various transformation conditions (Hanahan, 1983).
For this experiment, the most likely problem would be with transformation. It could be
optimized and modified by making changes mentioned below:
a. Temperature and duration: Confirm that the heat shock conditions (e.g. 42°C for 30-45
seconds) are appropriate for your cells (Inoue et al., 1990).
b. Recovery duration: Allow adequate time (usually 1 hour) for the cells to recover and express
the antibiotic resistance marker (Sorek et al., 2013).
c. Optimal antibiotic concentration: Ensure the appropriate concentration of streptomycin for
selection is used on the plates. Too high or low of a concentration may result in inadequate
selection (Chen & Dubnau, 2004).
Part B write up 16
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
In addition to the technical challenges faced during the genomic library construction, human
errors could also have contributed to the unsuccessful or inconclusive results. These errors can
occur in sample handling, reagent preparation, equipment usage, and protocol execution. Such
errors may include:
1. Cross-contamination: During handling of samples, there is potential for cross-contamination
between different DNA samples or between the samples and reagents, leading to undesired
results (Inoue et al., 1990).
2. Reagent preparation: Errors can occur while preparing various reagents such as buffers,
enzyme solutions, or antibiotics. These could include inaccurate measurement or mixing of
components, resulting in incorrect concentrations that can affect experimental outcomes
(Sorek et al., 2013).
3. Pipetting errors: Inaccurate pipetting can lead to incorrect volumes being dispensed, resulting
in the incorrect sample or reagent concentration, which affects the outcome of experiments
(Hanahan, 1983).
4. Equipment usage: Improper operation, maintenance, or calibration of laboratory equipment
can generate unreliable or inconsistent results. For instance, inaccurate temperature settings
for incubation or heat shock can affect the transformation efficiency (Chen & Dubnau, 2004).
To minimize human errors, it is essential to maintain good laboratory practices, maintaining
proper organization of the workspace, labeling samples accurately, and double-checking
reagent concentrations. Additionally, regularly calibrating and maintaining equipment,
following established protocols carefully, and incorporating appropriate controls into
experiments will help reduce the occurrence of human errors and enhance the overall success
of the genomic library construction process.
Future experiments can investigate alternative restriction enzymes, plasmid vectors, and
competent cell strains to improve the overall success of the genomic library construction
process (Cirino et al., 2003). Moreover, ensuring a suitable recovery time for transformed cells,
providing a nutrient-rich medium during recovery, using appropriate plating methods and
conditions, and including positive and negative controls in each transformation experiment will
aid in enhancing the efficiency of the genomic library construction and subsequent functional
selection of the streptomycin resistance-conferring rspL gene (Hanahan, 1983).
Conclusion
Part B write up 17
Jetul and Japneet April 9, 2023
In conclusion, the construction of a genomic library using E.coli Top10 genomic DNA and pUC19
plasmid DNA proved to be challenging due to several factors, including low DNA
concentrations, contamination, and inefficient transformation. Optimization of the
transformation process, selection of alternative restriction enzymes, plasmid vectors, and
competent cell strains could enhance the overall success of the genomic library construction
and subsequent functional selection of the streptomycin resistance-conferring rspL gene.
Future experiments should also emphasize proper controls, recovery conditions, and nutrientrich media to improve the efficiency of this process.

The research strategy for this proposed study on the effect of sales promotion on organizational performance, focusing on Nigeria Breweries Limited, will follow the research onion framework developed by Saunders et al. (2012). This framework suggests a systematic approach to research design by layering various methodological elements to create a comprehensive research plan.

In the outermost layer, the study's philosophical stance will be rooted in pragmatism. This approach acknowledges the existence of multiple realities and the importance of using both quantitative and qualitative data to understand complex phenomena like sales promotions and organizational performance. By adopting pragmatism as the research philosophy, the study will embrace a mixed-methods research strategy.

The subsequent layer, research approach, involves combining inductive and deductive reasoning to drive hypothesis formation and data collection. This dual approach will enable a thorough examination of sales promotion effectiveness and ethical considerations, as well as the development of a suitable training program for Nigeria Breweries Limited's marketing and sales teams.

Research Strategy (200 words):

The research design for this proposed study will be explanatory and exploratory in nature, incorporating both quantitative and qualitative data collection techniques. Explanatory research will aid in understanding the relationships between sales promotion strategies, organizational performance, and consumer behavior. In contrast, exploratory research will help discover new insights and investigate ethical considerations, innovative techniques, and training program development.

Quantitative data will be collected through the analysis of secondary data, such as financial reports, to assess the impact of sales promotion strategies on Nigeria Breweries Limited's financial performance (i.e., revenue, profit margins, and market share) over a period of three years. Additionally, questionnaires will be administered to a sample of employees within the organization's marketing and sales teams to gather information on their experiences with promotional activities, ethical concerns, and training needs.

Qualitative data will be obtained through semi-structured interviews with key stakeholders, such as managers and executives, to explore their perspectives on sales promotion strategies, ethical considerations, and the potential for innovative promotion techniques. These interviews will provide in-depth insights into the organizational culture, decision-making processes, and the potential for creating a comprehensive training program tailored to the firm's needs.

By employing a mixed-methods research design, the study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the effect of sales promotion on Nigeria Breweries Limited's performance and contribute valuable knowledge to the beverage industry, marketing professionals, educators, and policymakers.
